title: Derived quasi-coherent etale-Zariski equivalence and pullback comparison
statement:
Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Write $\epsilon_T:(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})\to(T_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_T)$ for the canonical ringed-site morphism, whose direct image is restriction to open subschemes and whose module pullback is $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon_T^{-1}\mathcal O_T}\epsilon_T^{-1}(-)$ [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. All sites are taken small relative to the universe of their module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention]. Module derived categories are the unbounded localizations of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On a ringed site, a perfect object means one locally isomorphic in that derived category to a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free structure modules. A quasi-coherent module on an algebraic space is as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ denotes the full subcategory of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. Zariski quasi-coherence means locally an associated module sheaf [pqf-def-coherent]. The functor $\epsilon_T^*$ is exact and faithful on all module sheaves. It induces an equivalence
$$\epsilon_T^*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}),$$
with quasi-inverse $R\epsilon_{T,*}$ and with the canonical derived adjunction unit and counit as its equivalence comparisons. For every scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\epsilon_{T'}^*Lh^*\simeq Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_T^*$$
on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$. It is the derived pullback comparison induced by the commuting square of ringed topoi; on tensor representatives it sends iterated scalar extension to scalar extension along the composite. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme morphism $h$, the equivalence also intertwines $Rh_*$ and $Rh_{\mathrm{et},*}$. The pullback comparisons commute with the canonical identity and composition comparisons and identify the structure modules and their scalar-insertion maps.

source.place: Tags 08H8 (lemma-epsilon-flat), 071Q (lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site), including its quasi-inverse and counit proof, and 08GH (remark-match-total-direct-images); tensor normalization from descent.tex Tag 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites).

proof.text: Start with a short exact sequence of arbitrary Zariski modules. At $x\in T$, its stalk sequence is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]. By [lem-sfb-etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk], the geometric stalk of its termwise $\epsilon_T^*$ image is the tensor of this stalk sequence with $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ over $R=\mathcal O_{T,x}$. This tensor sequence is exact by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] and [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. To conclude sheaf exactness, forget module structure using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], the geometric stalk of the homology sheaf of the image sequence is the homology of its stalk sequence, hence zero. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], the map from that homology sheaf to zero is an isomorphism. Faithful exact forgetting then says its module homology is zero as well. This applies at each position, so $\epsilon_T^*$ is exact on all modules.

If $\epsilon_T^*M=0$, [lem-sfb-etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk] gives $M_x\otimes_RR^{\mathrm{sh}}=0$. Every $x$ admits a geometric lift by choosing an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Faithful flatness [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat, def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], applied to $0\to M_x\to0$, implies $M_x=0$. The exactness test [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5), applied to $0\to M\to0$, gives $M=0$. If $\epsilon_T^*u=0$, exactness from step 1 gives $\epsilon_T^*(\operatorname{im}u)=\operatorname{im}(\epsilon_T^*u)=0$, so $\operatorname{im}u=0$ and $u=0$. Apply this to differences of maps to obtain faithfulness.

source.place: 08H8, zero detection, followed by the image argument for faithfulness.

proof.text: Use the canonical unbounded derived adjunction $\epsilon_T^*\dashv R\epsilon_{T,*}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; here $L\epsilon_T^*=\epsilon_T^*$ because step 1 shows exactness. The ordinary QCoh equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies tensor pullback with associated etale modules and restriction with its inverse, with their ordinary unit and counit. Thus $H^q(\epsilon_T^*F)=\epsilon_T^*H^q(F)$ is quasi-coherent whenever $H^q(F)$ is. This defines the left functor on the desired full subcategories, without imposing quasi-coherence on terms of a representative.

source.place: 071Q, first paragraph and ordinary QCoh comparison.

proof.text: Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})$ and write $N^q=H^q(E)$. The affine etale objects form a covering basis: cover the source scheme of any etale object by affine opens, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. On an affine object $u:U\to T$, $N^q|_U$ is the etale extension of a quasi-coherent Zariski module, by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. The localized site is $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]. Therefore [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives vanishing of its positive abelian cohomology; [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice] gives the identical vanishing for module-derived evaluation. All sites are small, and enough injectives follows from [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-acyclic-basis-cohomology] to obtain $H^q(R\Gamma(U,E))\cong N^q(U)$, naturally in $E$ and in affine etale $U$. No lower bound on $E$ has been used.

Choose $E\to I$ K-injective by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and step 1, $\epsilon_{T,*}I$ is K-injective: a map from acyclic $A$ to it is adjoint, including homotopies, to a map $\epsilon_T^*A\to I$, hence is null-homotopic. It represents $R\epsilon_{T,*}E$. On an affine open $W$, its section complex is $I(W)$, since $\epsilon_{T,*}$ is restriction. The module presheaf homology is consequently $W\mapsto H^q(I(W))$. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] identifies its sheafification with $H^q(\epsilon_{T,*}I)$. Step 4 identifies this presheaf on the affine-open basis with $W\mapsto N^q(W)$. These identifications commute with restriction. Sheafifying therefore gives
$$H^q(R\epsilon_{T,*}E)\cong\epsilon_{T,*}N^q.$$
The right side is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Thus the right derived functor also restricts to the asserted full subcategory.

source.place: 071Q, cohomology of derived restriction; derived.tex 08BJ adjunction argument.

proof.text:
Under step 5 and exact pullback, the cohomology of the canonical derived counit is the ordinary counit
$$\epsilon_T^*\epsilon_{T,*}N^q\longrightarrow N^q.$$
Indeed the step-4 comparison is the canonical edge map: on the affine basis a class in $H^q(I(U))$ maps to its section in $H^q(E)(U)$, and counit evaluation applies the same restriction and scalar multiplication as the ordinary module adjunction. This follows on local cycle representatives and respects boundaries and restriction. The counit is an isomorphism by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Hence the derived counit is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree, and therefore an isomorphism. For the derived unit $\eta_F:F\to R\epsilon_{T,*}\epsilon_T^*F$, the triangle identity says its image under $\epsilon_T^*$ is inverse to that counit. Step 2 and exactness imply that $\epsilon_T^*$ reflects zero cohomology (apply zero detection to each $H^q$), hence reflects quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $\eta_F$ is also an isomorphism. The specified adjunction, restricted using steps 3 and 5, now supplies the equivalence with precisely its canonical unit and counit.

source.place: 071Q, its counit and unit arguments, with their maps specified.

proof.text:
For $h:T'\to T$, [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] identifies $\epsilon_{T,*}h_{\mathrm{et},*}$ with $h_*\epsilon_{T',*}$, including structural ring actions: on an open $W\subseteq T$, both give $G(h^{-1}W)$ with the same action. This is the ring-compatible square of topoi of 08GH. Apply the composition and 2-isomorphism comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to its two composites. They give
$$\epsilon_{T'}^*Lh^*\cong L( h\epsilon_{T'})^*\cong L(\epsilon_T h_{\mathrm{et}})^*\cong Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_T^*.$$
Here $L\epsilon^*=\epsilon^*$ by exactness in steps 1–2. The comparison is computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms, whose pullbacks remain K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus it is the derived comparison of the specified square, with the stated iterated-scalar-extension representative, and is natural on derived objects. The Zariski $Lh^*$ preserves quasi-coherent cohomology: [lem-pc-derived-pullback-qcoh-component] proves this on every affine source chart mapping into an affine target chart, and these charts cover $T'$. Step 6 and the comparison then show preservation on the etale side as well.

source.place: 08GH, remark-match-total-direct-images, first diagram; 03FH(2) and derived ringed-topos composition.

proof.text: Suppose $h:T'\to T$ is qcqs. Zariski $Rh_*$ preserves quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. On the etale side, restrict to an affine open $W\subseteq T$ and set $V=h^{-1}W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $V$ is qcqs, since $h$ is qcqs and $W$ is affine. The preservation clause of [lem-sfb-space-derived-pushforward-coproducts] applies to $V\to W$, as a map between qcqs representable algebraic spaces over $W$. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], restriction of $Rh_{\mathrm{et},*}$ to $W$ is $R(h|_V)_{\mathrm{et},*}$ and quasi-coherence of cohomology is local on the target. Its preservation on all such $W$ proves preservation for $h_{\mathrm{et}}$. This uses no global quasi-compactness assumption on $T$.

source.place: 08GH, second diagram: preservation of its four quasi-coherent subcategories.

proof.text:
The ring-compatible square in step 7, together with the derived composition and 2-isomorphism comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], gives
$$\Psi:R\epsilon_{T,*}Rh_{\mathrm{et},*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*R\epsilon_{T',*}.$$
For $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{T'})$, define the comparison as the composite
$$\epsilon_T^*Rh_*F\xrightarrow{\epsilon_T^*Rh_*\eta_F}\epsilon_T^*Rh_*R\epsilon_{T',*}\epsilon_{T'}^*F\xrightarrow{\epsilon_T^*\Psi^{-1}}\epsilon_T^*R\epsilon_{T,*}Rh_{\mathrm{et},*}\epsilon_{T'}^*F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}Rh_{\mathrm{et},*}\epsilon_{T'}^*F.$$
Step 6 makes the first arrow invertible, the middle arrow is the composition comparison, and steps 6 and 8 make the final counit invertible. Thus this is a natural isomorphism. The cited composition comparisons identify the specified composite adjunctions, so the displayed unit-composition-counit formula is the canonical comparison for the given square. This proves the qcqs direct-image clause without using [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison], whose newly landed proof depends on this item.

source.place: 08GH, second square and its R epsilon_* proof, with the comparison map expanded.

proof.text: Check the remaining normalization on the K-flat representatives allowed in step 7. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], all comparisons there come from ordinary pullback composition and preserve the tensor unit. Locally, ordinary composition contracts $c\otimes b\otimes m$ to $c\,h^{\sharp}(b)\otimes m$. For three scalar extensions, either parenthesization sends $d\otimes c\otimes b\otimes m$ to $d\,k^{\sharp}(c)\,(kh)^{\sharp}(b)\otimes m$, by associativity and the ring-map identity. Inserting an identity extension sends $1\otimes m$ to $m$; the inverse inserts $1$. These formulas are compatible with restriction and the balancing relations, so give equal sheaf maps and equal maps of complexes. Localizing gives the identity and composition compatibilities for step 7 on all derived objects. For the structure module the same formula is scalar multiplication, and it takes every scalar insertion $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ to that of the composite. Consequently the comparison identifies the prescribed structure modules and scalar-insertion maps.

split_report.summary: Repaired a live-induced cycle by proving exactness from geometric stalks and 071Q from the acyclic affine basis, rather than citing the dependent scheme-derived comparison. Added the general ringed-site 0BKZ input; derived both 08GH comparisons with their canonical maps. Item statement unchanged. Maintenance 2026-10-24 (Q38): step 8 now cites the existing 08FA preservation clause of lem-sfb-space-derived-pushforward-coproducts.
